label: October 2026

biggest.lede: We move the clock closer to midnight by one second as worsening Ebola outbreak and severe Australian storms increase immediate biological and climate risks.

title: Ebola Outbreak Pushes Clock closer to midnight
summary: The clock started October at 85 seconds and ended at 84 seconds, moving closer to midnight due to a worsening Ebola outbreak and severe storms in Australia. The single biggest driver was the surge in Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo, which raised biological and climate risk assessments.

sections.heading: What moved the clock
body: On October 31 the clock was moved closer to midnight one second from 85 to 84 seconds. Experts cited a worsening Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with deaths exceeding 5,000 and fears of regional spread, as a key biological risk. Severe storms in Australia were also noted as increasing immediate climate risk, reinforcing the decision to move the clock closer to midnight.

sections.heading: Where the experts disagreed
body: There were no days in October where experts voted in opposite directions; all votes were either hold or worse, so no disagreement occurred.

sections.heading: What to watch next month
body: Monitor the trajectory of the Ebola outbreak in Central Africa and any further developments in Australian extreme weather, as both could influence biological and climate risk assessments for November.
